claims.text: Melt-spinning can produce amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 ribbons.
The melt-spun Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 ribbon has a homogeneous, grain-free amorphous microstructure.
Room-temperature Ar+ irradiation at 10^14–10^15 ions/cm^2 remains below the threshold for macroscopic damage in this alloy.
Low-dose ion irradiation of the amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 ribbon produces point defects.
The irradiation produces a spatially homogeneous population of point defects in the amorphous ribbon.
Irradiation-induced point defects and slight atomic displacements disrupt medium-range ordering in the amorphous alloy.
The induced defects increase atomic disorder.
Increased disorder interferes with cooperative atomic rearrangements required for crystallization and raises the crystallization nucleation barrier.
Low-dose irradiation will increase the DSC-measured crystallization onset temperature relative to an unirradiated control.
Low-dose post-melt-spinning irradiation will improve the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
Low-dose irradiation applied after melt-spinning will improve the alloy's glass-forming ability.
The beneficial irradiation treatment can preserve the overall amorphous structure without producing nanocrystallites.
Exceeding the optimal ion dose may create nonuniform defect concentrations, nucleation sites, or damage to the amorphous structure.
The unirradiated melt-spun alloy has moderate thermal stability and a standard crystallization onset temperature.

contradictions.description: The intervention is applied only after melt-spinning has already formed an amorphous ribbon, yet it is claimed to improve glass-forming ability. Post-formation changes in crystallization resistance can test amorphous-state stability, but they do not directly alter or measure the ability to form the original glass.

Enhanced glass-forming ability is a predicted outcome, but the experiment measures crystallization onset and preservation of an already amorphous structure; it does not measure a glass-forming metric such as critical cooling rate, critical casting thickness, or amorphous yield under matched processing.
